    Compute Single-Cell Level Scores (c_i)

    get_cs.Rd

    The cell score is a weighted average of the raw S-LDSC enrichment estimates, cs_i = sum_k w_ik ehat_k with w_ik = l_ik s_k / sum_k l_ik s_k, so the weights sum to one and the score equals 1 when no topic is enriched. The enrichments are used without shrinkage. The z-score tests cs_i = 1 (no enrichment in the cell's open regions relative to genome-wide).

    get_cs(
  topic_res,
  ldsc_res_dir,
  trait,
  nTopics,
  baseline_prefix = NULL,
  frq_prefix = NULL,
  Sigma = NULL,
  use_approximation = FALSE,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater"),
  min_pct_blocks = 1.7,
  block_coverage = NULL,
  small_annot = c("floor", "warn"),
  min_prop_snps = NULL,
  fdr_alpha = 0.05,
  fdr_draws = 1000,
  fdr_seed = 1,
  chrs = 1:22
)

    Arguments

    topic_res

    Results from run_fastTopics_res, with Pmat (J×K) and Lmat (I×K)

    ldsc_res_dir

    Directory containing k*_output/results/Trait.results

    trait

    Trait name used in LDSC results files.

    nTopics

    Number of topics (K).

    baseline_prefix, frq_prefix

    Prefixes of the baseline annotation and PLINK frequency files, matching the --ref-ld-chr and --frqfile-chr of the S-LDSC runs. These are used to build the covariance of the enrichment estimates with ldsc_jackknife_cov(), which is the default.

    Sigma

    Optional K x K covariance matrix of the enrichment estimates, supplied directly instead of being computed.

    use_approximation

    Use the annotation-correlation approximation Cov(e_k, e_k') ~ w_k w_k' Cor(A_k, A_k') instead of the jackknife covariance. Default FALSE; the jackknife is preferred, and one of Sigma, the reference prefixes, or this flag must be given.

    alternative

    Either "two.sided" (default, preserving previous behaviour) or "greater" for a one-sided test of enrichment. Under "two.sided", cells that are significantly depleted (z < 0) also pass FDR; if the scores are presented as disease relevance, "greater" is usually the intended test.

    min_pct_blocks

    Minimum percentage of the genome's 0.01 cM blocks a topic annotation must overlap (see Small annotations). Default 1.7.

    block_coverage

    Optional precomputed coverage: the data frame returned by annot_block_coverage(), or a numeric vector of pct_blocks of length K. Computed from baseline_prefix when NULL.

    small_annot

    What to do with topics below min_pct_blocks: "floor" (default) floors them as described in Details; "warn" keeps them. Both warn.

    min_prop_snps

    Deprecated. If given, the previous rule (floor topics with S-LDSC Prop._SNPs below this fraction) is used instead of block coverage.

    fdr_alpha

    BH level defining the significant cells ranked by the rank FDR. Default 0.05.

    fdr_draws

    Number of enrichment draws for the rank FDR. Default 1000. Set to 0 to skip it.

    fdr_seed

    Random seed for the rank FDR draws. Default 1.

    chrs

    Chromosomes the S-LDSC runs used, for the jackknife covariance and the block coverage. Default 1:22.

    Value

    A list with

    • cs: cell scores (vector of length I)

    • z_cell: z-score accounting for variance

    • p_cell: p-value for assessing score reliability, length I, NA where the variance is zero or non-finite

    • var_cell: cell score variance used in the denominator of z

    • Sigma_used: the K x K covariance actually used

    • ldsc_res_table: the raw tau_display table from S-LDSC

    • rank_fdr: resolvable-error rank FDR of the significant cells, as returned by rank_fdr() (curve, mean_fdr, fdr_top10, n_sig, sig); NULL if fdr_draws = 0

    • cs_dat: intermediate estimates for calculating cell score, including the normalised cell topic weights W and the floored-topic indicator drop

    • topic_qc: one row per topic with the S-LDSC enrichment, Prop._SNPs, pct_blocks, small (below the size threshold), negative (negative enrichment) and floored

    Details

    Two filtering rules are applied to the S-LDSC estimates before they enter the score. A topic whose estimated enrichment is negative, or whose annotation is too small for S-LDSC's p-values to control type I error (below), is floored to e_k = 1 with w_k = 0. Such topics contribute nothing to the numerator and nothing to the variance, but they remain in the weight denominator, so the effect is to dilute the score toward 1 rather than to renormalise over the retained topics. This is deliberate and conservative.

    Small annotations

    For small annotations S-LDSC's block-jackknife p-values do not control type I error: the tail of very small p-values is inflated (Tashman et al. 2021). Following that paper, an annotation is judged by the percentage of the genome's 0.01 cM blocks it overlaps, which reflects both its size and how clustered it is (see annot_block_coverage()). Topics overlapping fewer than min_pct_blocks percent (default 1.7, the paper's threshold for the one-sided and enrichment tests) are reported in a warning and, with small_annot = "floor" (default), floored. With small_annot = "warn" they are kept, and the warning is the only safeguard.

    Block coverage needs the reference SNPs' genetic map positions, read from baseline_prefix, or a precomputed block_coverage. Without either, the previous rule is used instead, flooring topics with S-LDSC Prop._SNPs below 0.5%, and a message says so.

    The reliability of the cell ranking is summarised by the resolvable-error rank FDR (rank_fdr()), computed among the significant cells (one-sided BH < fdr_alpha) from the enrichments and Sigma.

    References

    Tashman KC, Cui R, O'Connor LJ, Neale BM, Finucane HK (2021). Significance testing for small annotations in stratified LD-Score regression. medRxiv 2021.03.13.21249938.

    See also

    ldsc_jackknife_cov(), annot_block_coverage(), rank_fdr()
